turns.user: Inverse-design a printable mortar: 28-day compressive strength >= 40 MPa and static yield stress between 1 and 4 kPa, minimising the clinker fraction. Search space: OPC required 0.5-1.0, silica fume 0-0.15, limestone powder 0-0.3, w/b 0.28-0.45. Run without asking.
turns.text:
I’ll run the inverse design over your specified search space, minimising OPC fraction as the available proxy for clinker content, then check the candidates and their published analogues.
The initial search returned low-OPC candidates, but their median yield stresses fall below your requested range. I’ll tighten the rheology screening to check whether the same search space offers a more convincing candidate. Assumptions are fixed sand/binder ratio, moist curing, standard cube testing, and no added admixtures.
**The search found a low-clinker trial candidate, but did not establish a mortar meeting both targets reliably.**

Best candidate from the initial search:

| Parameter | Result |
|---|---:|
| OPC binder fraction | 0.70 |
| Limestone powder fraction | 0.30 |
| Silica fume | Absent |
| w/b | 0.302 |
| s/b | 1.50 |
| Compressive strength | **47.73 [27.22, 69.89] MPa** |
| Static yield stress | **787 [19, 4,181] Pa** |

Predictions are q50 [q10, q90]. The engine reports clinker fraction **0.70**, effectively an OPC-fraction proxy here; actual cement clinker content was not supplied.

The strength target has predicted satisfaction probability **0.69**, and the yield-stress target **0.36**. Median yield stress misses your lower limit. Tightening rheology probability to **0.50** produced **no feasible candidates before automatic threshold relaxation**; the relaxed result is not a successful design.

Defaults used: moist curing, `comp_cube50`, s/b **1.50**, no admixtures, printing context enabled, and static yield assessed at rest time **0 s**.

Published evidence provides stronger starting references: [Mixture A](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2017.12.112) reports **49.7 MPa** and **3,350 Pa**; [RFA-50](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2025.144187) reports **44.6 MPa** and **1,760 Pa**. Both lie outside your permitted binder space.

Treat the rheology prediction as order-of-magnitude guidance. Printability remains unverified without geometry and printing schedule; final selection requires experiments.
